The chief priests, however, resolved to put Lazarus to death as well, because on his account many of the Jews were leaving them and believing in Jesus. The king comes to Jerusalem The next day the large crowd that had come for the festival heard that Jesus was on his way into Jerusalem. They took branches from the palm trees and went out to meet him. They were shouting, “Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord, Israel’s King!” Jesus found a young donkey and sat on it, just as Scripture says: “Do not be afraid, daughter of Zion! Look, your king is coming, sitting on a donkey’s colt.” At first his disciples did not understand what these things meant. But when Jesus had been glorified, they remembered that these things had been written about him, and that they had done these very things for him. Meanwhile the crowd that had been with him when he called Lazarus out of his tomb and raised him from the dead kept on testifying to what they had seen. That was also why the crowd went out to meet him: they had heard that he had done this sign. So the Pharisees said to one another, “You can see for yourselves that you are getting nowhere. Look, the whole world has gone off after him!” The hour has come Among those who went up to worship at the festival were some Greeks. These men came to Philip, whose home was Bethsaida in Galilee, and made a request of him: “Sir, we would like to see Jesus.” Philip went and told Andrew, and then Andrew and Philip went and told Jesus. Jesus answered them, “The hour has come when the Son of Man is to be glorified. Truly, truly, I tell you, if a grain of wheat does not fall into the ground and die, it stays just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit. Whoever loves their life is losing it, and whoever hates their life in this world will keep it safe for eternal life. Anyone who serves me must follow me, and my servant will be where I am. The Father will honor anyone who serves me. Now my soul is troubled, and what should I say? Father, save me from this hour. But it was for this very reason that I came to this hour. Father, glorify your name.” Then a voice came out of heaven: “I have glorified it and will glorify it again.” The crowd that stood there and heard it said it had thundered. Others were saying, “An angel has spoken to him.” Jesus answered, “This voice came for your sake, not for mine. Now is the time of judgment for this world; now the ruler of this world will be driven out. As for me, when I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw all people to myself.” He said this to show what kind of death he was going to die. The crowd answered him, “We have heard from the Law that the Christ remains forever. So how can you tell us that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?” So Jesus told them, “The light is among you for only a little while longer. Walk while you have the light, so that darkness does not overtake you. Anyone who walks in the darkness does not know where they are going. While you have the light, believe in the light, and so become children of light.” Why many did not believe When Jesus had said these things, he went away and hid himself from them. Although Jesus had done so many signs before their eyes, they did not believe in him. It happened this way so that the word the prophet Isaiah spoke would be fulfilled: “Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the Lord’s arm been revealed?” This is why they could not believe, because in another place Isaiah said: “He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, so that they would not see with their eyes, and understand with their heart, and turn, and I would heal them.” Isaiah said these things because he saw his glory and spoke about him. Even so, many even among the rulers believed in him. But because of the Pharisees they would not say so openly, so that they would not be expelled from the synagogue. For they loved the glory that people give more than the glory that God gives. Then Jesus called out, “Anyone who believes in me believes not just in me, but in the one who sent me. And anyone who sees me sees the one who sent me. I have come as a light into the world, so that whoever believes in me will not remain in the darkness. If anyone hears my words but does not keep them, I do not condemn them. For I did not come to condemn the world, but to save the world. Anyone who rejects me and does not accept my words has a judge: the very word I have spoken will judge them on the last day. For I have not spoken on my own authority; the Father who sent me has himself given me a commandment about what to say and what to speak. And I know that his commandment is eternal life. So whatever I say, I say just as the Father has told me.”

fields.title: John 13
fields.body_html:
Jesus washes the disciples’ feet

It was just before the Passover festival. Jesus knew that his hour had come, the hour for him to pass from this world to the Father. He had loved his own who were in the world, and he loved them to the end. Supper was under way, and the devil had already put the thought of betraying Jesus into the heart of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot. Jesus knew that the Father had put everything into his hands. He knew too that he had come out from God and was on his way back to God. He got up from the meal, put aside his outer garments, took a towel and tied it around his waist. Next he poured water into the basin and began washing the disciples’ feet, drying them with the towel he had tied around himself. He came to Simon Peter. Peter said to him, “Lord, are you going to wash my feet?” Jesus answered him, “You do not know yet what I am doing, but after this you will come to know it.” Peter said to him, “You are never going to wash my feet, not ever!” Jesus answered him, “If I do not wash you, you can have no share with me.” Simon Peter said to him, “Then, Lord, not just my feet! My hands and my head as well!” Jesus said to him, “Anyone who has bathed needs nothing more than to wash the feet, and is clean all over. And you are clean, yet not all of you.” For he knew who was going to betray him; this is the reason he said, “Not all of you are clean.”

An example to follow

When Jesus had washed their feet, he put his outer clothes back on and took his place at the table. Then he spoke to them again: “Do you understand what I have done for you? You call me ‘Teacher’ and ‘Lord,’ and you are right, because that is what I am. So if I, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, then you too have a duty to wash each other’s feet. What I gave you was an example, so that you also would do as I have done for you. Truly, truly, I tell you, a servant is not greater than his master, and one who is sent is not greater than the one who sent him. Now you know these things; you are blessed if you act on them. I am not speaking of all of you. I know the ones I chose. But it is happening so that the Scripture may be fulfilled: ‘The one who eats my bread has raised his heel against me.’ From now on I am telling you before it happens, so that when it does happen you will believe that I am. Truly, truly, I tell you, anyone who welcomes someone I send welcomes me, and anyone who welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me.”

One of you will betray me

After saying this, Jesus was troubled in spirit, and he solemnly declared, “Truly, truly, I tell you, one of you is going to betray me.” The disciples looked at one another, puzzled, unable to tell which of them he meant. One of his disciples, the disciple whom Jesus loved, was reclining close beside him. So Simon Peter signaled to him to find out who it could be that he meant. Leaning back against Jesus’s chest as he lay, the disciple asked him, “Lord, who is it?” Jesus answered, “I will dip this piece of bread and give it to someone; he is the one.” So he dipped the bread and gave it to Judas, son of Simon Iscariot. Once Judas had received the bread, Satan entered into him. So Jesus told him, “Do quickly what you are doing.” But none of those at the table understood what he meant by saying this to him. Since Judas kept the money box, some thought Jesus was telling him, “Buy what we need for the festival,” or that he was to give something to the poor. So once he had taken the piece of bread, Judas went straight out. And it was night.

A new commandment

When Judas had gone out, Jesus said, “The Son of Man has now been glorified, and in him God has been glorified. If God has been glorified in him, God will glorify him in himself as well, and he will do it without delay. Little children, I am with you for only a short time more. You will search for me, and what I said to the Jews I now say to you as well: ‘You cannot come where I am going.’ I am giving you a new commandment: love one another. In the same way that I have loved you, you too must love one another. If you have love for one another, everyone will know by this that you are my disciples.”

Peter’s denial foretold

Simon Peter asked him, “Lord, where are you going?” Jesus answered, “You cannot follow me now to the place where I am going, but later you will follow.” Peter said to him, “Lord, why can I not follow you right now? I will lay down my life for you.” Jesus answered, “Will you really lay down your life for me? Truly, truly, I tell you, no rooster will crow before you have denied me three times.”

fields.title: John 14
fields.body_html:
The way to the Father

“Do not let your hearts be troubled. Believe in God, and believe in me as well. There are many dwelling places in my Father’s house. Otherwise I would have told you, for I am going to prepare a place for you. And when I have gone and prepared a place for you, I will come back and take you to be with me, so that you also may be where I am. And you know the way that leads to where I am going.” Thomas said to him, “Lord, we do not know where you are going. Then how are we to know the way?” Jesus answered him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. Only through me does anyone come to the Father. Had you known me, you would have known my Father too. And from now on you know him; you have seen him.”

Whoever has seen me has seen the Father

Philip said to him, “Lord, show us the Father; we will need nothing more.” Jesus said to him, “I have been with you all this time, Philip, and you still do not know me? To have seen me is to have seen the Father. So how is it that you say, ‘Show us the Father’? Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and that the Father is in me? The words I say to you are not spoken on my own authority. Rather, the Father who remains in me is doing his works. Believe me: I am in the Father, and the Father is in me. If not, then believe because of the works themselves. Truly, truly, I tell you, anyone who believes in me will also do the works I am doing, and will do greater works than these, since I am going to the Father. And whatever you ask in my name, I will do it, so that in the Son the Father may be glorified. If you ask me anything in my name, I myself will do it.

The promise of the Advocate

If you love me, you will keep the commandments I have given you. I will ask the Father, and in answer he will give you another Advocate, who will be with you forever. This is the Spirit of truth. The world is not able to receive him, since it does not see him and does not know him. But you know him, for he remains with you, and he will be in you.

I will not leave you like orphans with no father; I am coming to you. In a short time the world will no longer see me, but you will see me. Because I live, you too will live. On that day you will come to know that I am in my Father, and that you are in me and I am in you. Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, that person is the one who loves me. Whoever loves me will be loved by my Father; I in turn will love them and show myself to them.” Judas (not Judas Iscariot) said to him, “Lord, how is it that you will show yourself to us, but not to the world?” Jesus replied, “Anyone who loves me will keep my word. My Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our dwelling place with them. Anyone who does not love me does not keep my words. And the word you are hearing is not mine; it belongs to the Father who sent me.

Peace I leave with you

I have told you these things while I am still with you. But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father is going to send in my name, is the one who will teach you everything and remind you of all I have said to you. Peace I leave with you; it is my own peace that I give you. I do not give the way the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not let them give way to fear. You heard me tell you, ‘I am leaving, and I am coming back to you.’ If you loved me, you would be glad I am going to the Father, for the Father is greater than I am. I have told you now, before it takes place, so that when it does take place you will believe. I will not say much more to you, for the ruler of the world is coming. He has no hold on me. But so that the world will know that I love the Father, I do exactly as the Father has commanded me.

Get up; let us go from here.

fields.title: John 15
fields.body_html:
The true vine

I am the true vine, and my Father is the vine grower. He takes away any branch in me that bears no fruit, and he prunes clean every branch that does bear fruit, so that it will bear more fruit. Because of the word I have spoken to you, you are clean already. Remain in me, and I will remain in you. A branch cannot bear fruit by itself; it must remain in the vine. In the same way, you cannot bear fruit unless you remain in me. I am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever remains in me, with me remaining in them, is the one who bears much fruit, because you can do nothing apart from me. Anyone who does not remain in me is thrown out like a branch and dries up. People gather the branches, throw them into the fire, and they burn. If you remain in me and my words remain in you, ask for whatever you want, and it will be done for you. This is how my Father is glorified: that you bear much fruit and so prove to be my disciples. I have loved you just as the Father has loved me. Remain in my love. You will remain in my love if you keep my commandments, just as I have kept the commandments my Father gave me and remain in his love. I have said this to you so that my joy will be in you and your joy will be complete.

I have called you friends

My commandment is this: love one another in the same way that I have loved you. No one has a love greater than this: that someone lays down their life for their friends. You are my friends if you carry out what I command you. I do not call you servants any longer, since a servant is not aware of what his master is doing. I have called you friends instead, because I have made known to you everything I heard from my Father. You did not choose me; I chose you. I appointed you for this: to go and bear fruit, and for your fruit to remain, so that the Father may give you whatever you ask him in my name. I give you these commands so that you will love one another.

The world’s hatred

If the world hates you, know that it hated me before it hated you. If you belonged to the world, the world would love you as its own. But you do not belong to the world; I chose you out of the world, and that is why the world hates you. Remember the word I spoke to you: ‘A servant is not greater than his master.’ If they have persecuted me, they will persecute you too. If they have kept my word, they will keep yours too. But all this they will do to you on account of my name, because they do not know the one who sent me. Had I not come and spoken to them, they would have no sin. But as it is, they have no excuse for their sin. Whoever hates me hates my Father as well. Had I not done among them works that no one else has done, they would have no sin. But as it is, they have seen, and they have hated, both me and my Father. But this has happened so that the word written in their Law would be fulfilled: ‘They hated me for no reason.’

The Advocate will testify

The Advocate, whom I will send to you from the Father, is the Spirit of truth, who comes out from the Father. When he comes, he will testify about me. And you also testify about me, because you have been with me from the beginning.

fields.title: John 16
fields.body_html:
Warning of persecution

I have told you all this so that you will not stumble and fall away. They will expel you from the synagogue. In fact, an hour is coming when anyone who kills you will think they are doing God a sacred service. They will do these things because they have never known the Father or me. But I have said these things to you so that when the hour for them comes, you will remember that I told you of them.

The work of the Advocate

I did not tell you these things at the start, because I was with you. But now I am going to the one who sent me, and not one of you asks me, ‘Where are you going?’ Instead, sorrow has filled your hearts because I have said these things to you. But I am telling you the truth: my going away is to your advantage. For if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you at all; but if I go, I will send him to you. When he comes, he will show the world to be in the wrong about sin, about righteousness and about judgment: about sin, because they do not believe in me; about righteousness, because I go to the Father and you will see me no longer; and about judgment, because the ruler of this world stands judged.

There is much more I have to tell you, but it is more than you can bear right now. But when he, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will guide you in all the truth. What he says will not come from himself; he will speak what he hears, and he will make known to you what is yet to come. He will glorify me, because he will receive from what is mine and make it known to you. Everything the Father has is mine. That is why I said that he will receive from what is mine and make it known to you.

Sorrow will turn to joy

In a little while you will no longer see me, and then after another little while you will see me.” Then some of his disciples said to one another, “What does he mean by telling us, ‘In a little while you will no longer see me, and then after another little while you will see me’? And what about ‘because I am going to the Father’?” So they kept saying, “What does he mean by ‘a little while’? We do not understand what he is talking about.” Jesus knew that they wanted to ask him about it, so he said to them, “Are you discussing with one another what I meant when I said, ‘In a little while you will no longer see me, and then after another little while you will see me’? Truly, truly, I tell you, you will weep and mourn aloud, but the world will rejoice. You will be full of sorrow, but your sorrow will become joy. When a woman is giving birth she has sorrow, because her hour has come. But once her child is born, she no longer remembers the anguish, for joy that a human being has been born into the world. So it is with you: now you have sorrow, but I will see you again. Then your hearts will rejoice, and no one takes your joy away from you. On that day you will not ask me any questions. Truly, truly, I tell you, if you ask the Father for anything, he will give it to you in my name. So far you have asked for nothing in my name. Ask and you will receive, so that your joy will be complete.

I have overcome the world

“I have used figures of speech in telling you these things. An hour is coming when I will no longer use them with you; I will tell you about the Father in plain words. On that day you will ask in my name, and I do not say that I will ask the Father on your behalf. For the Father himself loves you, since you have loved me and believed that I came out from God. fields.title: John 17
fields.body_html:
Jesus prays to be glorified

After Jesus had said these things, he raised his eyes toward heaven and prayed: “Father, the hour has come. Glorify your Son, so that the Son may glorify you. For you have given him authority over all people, in order that he may give eternal life to everyone you have given him. And eternal life is this: that they know you, the only true God, and the one you sent, Jesus Christ. I have glorified you on earth by completing the work that you gave me to do. So now, Father, glorify me yourself, at your side, with the glory that was mine with you before there was a world.

Jesus prays for his disciples

I have made your name known to the people you gave me from the world. They belonged to you, and you gave them to me; they have kept your word. Now they have come to know that all you have given me is from you. For I have passed on to them the words you gave me, and they have accepted them. They have come to know for certain that I came from you, and they believe that it was you who sent me. I am asking on their behalf. I am not asking on the world’s behalf, but on behalf of those whom you have given me, because they belong to you. All that is mine is yours, and all that is yours is mine, and I have been glorified in them. I am no longer in the world, but they are still in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, keep them in your name, the name you have given me, so that they may be one, just as we are one. While I was with them, I kept them in your name, the name you have given me. I guarded them, and not one of them was lost except the one doomed to be lost, so that the Scripture would be fulfilled. But now I am coming to you, and I speak these words while still in the world, so that within themselves they may have my joy complete. I have given your word to them, and the world has hated them, because they do not belong to the world, just as I do not belong to the world. I am not asking you to take them out of the world, but to keep them safe from the evil one. They do not belong to the world, just as I do not belong to the world. Set them apart for yourself by the truth; your word is truth. Just as you sent me into the world, I in the same way have sent them into the world. For their sake I set myself apart, so that they too may be set apart by the truth.

Jesus prays for all who will believe

I am not asking on behalf of these alone. My prayer is also for those who are going to believe in me through their message. Father, I ask that all of them may be one. Just as you are in me and I am in you, so may they too be in us, so that the world may come to believe that you sent me. The glory that you have given me I have given to them, so that they may be one just as we are one. I am in them and you are in me. So may they be brought to perfect oneness, and the world will know that you sent me and loved them just as you loved me. Father, all that you have given me: it is my will that they too may be with me where I am, to see my glory, which you gave me because you loved me before the world was founded.

Righteous Father, even though the world has never known you, I have known you, and these disciples have come to know that you sent me. I have made your name known to them, and I will go on making it known, so that the love you have had for me may be in them, and I in them.”

fields.title: John 18
fields.body_html:
Jesus is arrested

When Jesus had said these things, he went out with his disciples and crossed the Kidron Valley. A garden was there, and he and his disciples went into it. Judas, who was betraying him, also knew the place, since Jesus had often met there with his disciples. So Judas went there, bringing the detachment of soldiers and temple police sent by the chief priests and the Pharisees. They carried lanterns, torches and weapons. Jesus knew everything that was about to happen to him, so he went out to them and asked, “Who is it you are looking for?” They answered, “Jesus of Nazareth.” He said to them, “I am he.” Judas, who was betraying him, was standing there with them. When Jesus said to them, “I am he,” they stepped backward and fell to the ground. So he asked them again, “Who is it you are looking for?” “Jesus of Nazareth,” they said. Jesus replied, “I have told you that I am he. So if it is me you are looking for, let these men go.” This was so that his own word would be fulfilled: “I have not lost a single one of those you gave me.” Simon Peter had a sword. He pulled it out and struck the high priest’s servant, slicing off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus. Then Jesus told Peter, “Put your sword back in its sheath! Am I not to drink the cup that the Father has given me?” Then the detachment of soldiers with its commander, and the temple police sent by the Jewish leaders, arrested Jesus and tied him up. They took him first to Annas, the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year. It was Caiaphas who had advised the Jewish leaders that it would be better for one man to die for the people.

Peter denies Jesus

Simon Peter was following Jesus, and so was another disciple. That disciple was known to the high priest, and he went in with Jesus into the high priest’s courtyard. But Peter stood outside at the door. So the other disciple, the one known to the high priest, went out, spoke to the woman who kept the door, and brought Peter in. The servant girl who kept the door said to Peter, “You are not one of this man’s disciples too, are you?” He said, “I am not.” The servants and the temple police had made a charcoal fire, because it was cold, and they were standing around it warming themselves. Peter was standing with them too, warming himself.

Jesus before the high priest

Meanwhile the high priest began to question Jesus about his disciples and about his teaching. Jesus answered, “I have spoken openly to the world. I have always taught in synagogues and in the temple courts, where all the Jews come together. I have said nothing in secret. Why do you question me? Question those who heard what I said to them. Look, they know what I said.” When he had said this, one of the temple police who stood nearby slapped Jesus and said, “Is that the way you answer the high priest?” Jesus answered him, “If I said something wrong, then testify to what was wrong. But if I spoke rightly, why do you strike me?” Then Annas sent him on to Caiaphas the high priest, still bound.

Peter denies him again

Meanwhile Simon Peter was still standing there warming himself. So they said to him, “You are not one of his disciples too, are you?” He denied it and said, “I am not.” One of the high priest’s servants, a relative of the man whose ear Peter cut off, said, “Did I not see you with him in the garden?” Again Peter denied it, and at that moment a rooster crowed.

Jesus before Pilate

Then they led Jesus from Caiaphas to the governor’s headquarters. It was early morning. They did not go into the headquarters themselves, to avoid becoming ritually unclean, since they wanted to eat the Passover. So Pilate came outside to them and asked, “What charge are you making against this man?” They answered, “We would not have handed him over to you if this man were not a wrongdoer.” So Pilate told them, “You take him, then, and try him under your own law.” The Jewish leaders replied, “We are not permitted to execute anyone.” This was so that the word Jesus had spoken would be fulfilled, the word that showed what kind of death he was going to die.

My kingdom is not of this world

Then Pilate went back inside the headquarters. He called Jesus to him and asked, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus answered, “Are you asking this on your own, or have others told you about me?” Pilate answered, “Do you think I am a Jew? Your own nation and the chief priests are the ones who handed you over to me. What have you done?” Jesus answered, “My kingdom does not come from this world. If it did, my servants would be fighting to keep me from being handed over to the Jewish leaders. But as it is, my kingdom is not from here.” Pilate said to him, “So you are a king after all?” Jesus answered, “You are the one who says that I am a king. I was born for this, and I came into the world for this: to testify to the truth. All who belong to the truth listen to my voice.” Pilate said to him, “What is truth?” After saying this, he went back out to the Jewish leaders and told them, “I find no case against him. But you have a custom that I set one prisoner free for you at the Passover. So shall I set the King of the Jews free for you?” At that they shouted again, “Not this one! Barabbas!” Now Barabbas was a bandit.

fields.title: John 19
fields.body_html:
The soldiers mock Jesus

Then Pilate took Jesus and had him flogged. The soldiers wove a crown out of thorns and set it on his head, and they dressed him in a purple robe. Again and again they came up to him and said, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and struck him in the face. Pilate went outside again and said to them, “Look, I am bringing him out to you, so that you may know that I find no case against him.” So Jesus came outside, still wearing the thorny crown and the purple robe. Pilate said to them, “Look, here is the man!” When the chief priests and the temple police saw him, they shouted, “Crucify! Crucify!” Pilate told them, “Take him yourselves and crucify him. I find no case against him.” The Jewish leaders replied, “We have a law, and by that law he must die, because he made himself the Son of God.”

When Pilate heard this, he was even more afraid. He went back inside the headquarters and said to Jesus, “Where do you come from?” But Jesus gave him no answer. So Pilate said to him, “Are you refusing to speak to me?” Do you not know that I have authority to set you free and authority to crucify you? Jesus answered, “You would have no authority over me at all unless it had been given to you from above. That is why the one who handed me over to you carries the greater sin.” From then on Pilate tried to set him free, but the Jewish leaders shouted, “If you let this man go, you are no friend of Caesar. Anyone who claims to be a king is setting himself against Caesar.”

When Pilate heard this, he brought Jesus outside and took his seat on the judgment seat at the place known as the Stone Pavement, in Hebrew Gabbatha. It was the day of Preparation of the Passover, about noon. Pilate said to the Jewish leaders, “Look, here is your King!” They shouted back, “Away with him! Away with him! Crucify him!” Pilate said to them, “Shall I crucify your King?” The chief priests replied, “We have no king but Caesar.” Then Pilate handed him over to them to be crucified.

The crucifixion

So they took charge of Jesus. Carrying the cross by himself, he went out to what is called the Place of the Skull (in Hebrew, Golgotha). There they crucified him, along with two others, one on each side and Jesus in the middle. Pilate also wrote a notice and had it placed on the cross. The wording was: “Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews.” Many of the Jews of Jerusalem read this notice, since the spot where Jesus was crucified was close to the city. The notice was in Hebrew, Latin and Greek. The chief priests of the Jews objected. “Do not write ‘The King of the Jews,’” they told Pilate. “Write that this man said, ‘I am King of the Jews.’” Pilate answered, “What I have written, I have written.” When the soldiers had crucified Jesus, they took his clothes and divided them into four shares, one share for each soldier. They also took his tunic. The tunic was seamless, woven in a single piece from top to bottom. So they said to each other, “Let us not tear it. Let us cast lots for it and see who gets it.” This was so that the Scripture would be fulfilled that says, “They shared out my garments among themselves, and for my clothing they cast lots.”

That is what the soldiers did.

Jesus’s mother at the cross

Meanwhile, near the cross of Jesus stood his mother, her sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene. Jesus saw his mother there, and near her the disciple whom he loved. He said to his mother, “Woman, look, here is your son.” Then he said to the disciple, “Look, here is your mother.” From that time on the disciple took her into his own home.

The death of Jesus

After this, Jesus knew that everything had now been finished. So that the Scripture would be completed, he said, “I am thirsty.” A jar full of sour wine stood there. So they put a sponge soaked in the sour wine on a stalk of hyssop and raised it to his lips. When Jesus had taken the sour wine, he said, “It is finished.” Then he bowed his head and handed over his spirit.

Jesus’s side is pierced

It was the day of Preparation, and the Jewish leaders did not want the bodies to stay on the crosses over the Sabbath, because that Sabbath was a day of special importance. So they asked Pilate to have the men’s legs broken and the bodies removed. So the soldiers came. They broke the first man’s legs, and then the legs of the other man crucified with Jesus. But when they reached Jesus, they saw that he had already died. So they did not break his legs. One of the soldiers, however, drove a spear into his side, and at once blood and water flowed out. The one who saw this has testified to it, and his testimony is true. He knows that what he says is true, and he has told it so that you also may believe. These things took place so that the Scripture would be fulfilled: “Not one bone of his will be broken.” And another passage of Scripture also says, “They will look at the one they pierced.”

The burial of Jesus

After this, Joseph of Arimathea, a disciple of Jesus who had kept it hidden because he feared the Jewish leaders, asked Pilate for permission to take away the body of Jesus, and Pilate granted it. So Joseph came and took his body away. Nicodemus came too, the man who had first come to Jesus at night. He brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes weighing about 70 pounds. They took Jesus’s body and wrapped it with the spices in linen cloths, which is how the Jews prepare a body for burial. There was a garden at the place where he had been crucified, and in that garden there was a new tomb where no one had ever been laid. The tomb was close at hand, and it was the Jewish day of Preparation, so they laid Jesus there.

When Jesus had taken the sour wine, he said, “It is finished.” Then he bowed his head and handed over his spirit. Jesus’s side is pierced It was the day of Preparation, and the Jewish leaders did not want the bodies to stay on the crosses over the Sabbath, because that Sabbath was a day of special importance. So they asked Pilate to have the men’s legs broken and the bodies removed. So the soldiers came. They broke the first man’s legs, and then the legs of the other man crucified with Jesus. But when they reached Jesus, they saw that he had already died. So they did not break his legs. One of the soldiers, however, drove a spear into his side, and at once blood and water flowed out. The one who saw this has testified to it, and his testimony is true. He knows that what he says is true, and he has told it so that you also may believe. These things took place so that the Scripture would be fulfilled: “Not one bone of his will be broken.” And another passage of Scripture also says, “They will look at the one they pierced.” The burial of Jesus After this, Joseph of Arimathea, a disciple of Jesus who had kept it hidden because he feared the Jewish leaders, asked Pilate for permission to take away the body of Jesus, and Pilate granted it. So Joseph came and took his body away. Nicodemus came too, the man who had first come to Jesus at night. He brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes weighing about 70 pounds. They took Jesus’s body and wrapped it with the spices in linen cloths, which is how the Jews prepare a body for burial. There was a garden at the place where he had been crucified, and in that garden there was a new tomb where no one had ever been laid. The tomb was close at hand, and it was the Jewish day of Preparation, so they laid Jesus there.

fields.title: John 20
fields.body_html:
The empty tomb

On the first day of the week Mary Magdalene came to the tomb in the early morning, while it was still dark, and found that the stone had been taken away from it. She ran off, then, to find Simon Peter and the other disciple, whom Jesus loved. “They have removed the Lord from the tomb,” she told them, “and we do not know where they have laid him.” Peter and the other disciple then set out and made their way to the tomb. The two of them ran together, but the other disciple was faster than Peter and got to the tomb ahead of him. Bending down to look in, he saw the linen cloths lying there; he did not, however, go in. Then Simon Peter, who had been following him, came and went into the tomb. He saw the linen cloths lying there, and the face cloth that had been on his head. It was not lying with the linen cloths; it was rolled up in a place of its own, apart from them. Then the other disciple, who had arrived at the tomb first, went in too; and he saw and believed. For as yet they did not understand the Scripture, that he must rise from the dead. Then the disciples went back to where they were staying. Mary, however, stood outside the tomb, weeping. Still weeping, she stooped to look into the tomb. There she saw two angels in white clothes, sitting where the body of Jesus had been lying, one at the head, the other at the feet. They said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping?” “My Lord has been taken away,” she answered, “and I do not know where they have laid him.” With these words she turned around and saw Jesus standing there, though she did not know that it was Jesus. Jesus said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping? Who is it you are looking for?” Supposing he was the gardener, she said to him, “Sir, if you are the one who has carried him off, tell me where you put him, and I will take him away.” Jesus said to her, “Mary!” She turned and said to him in Hebrew, “Rabbouni!” (which means Teacher). Jesus said to her, “Do not keep holding on to me, because I have not yet ascended to the Father. Go instead to my brothers and sisters with this message: ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, my God and your God.’” Mary Magdalene went and brought the disciples the news: “I have seen the Lord!” And she reported to them what he had said to her.

Jesus appears to the disciples

On the evening of that day, the first day of the week, the disciples were behind locked doors because they feared the Jewish leaders. Jesus came and stood among them and said, “Peace to you.” After saying this, he showed them his hands and his side. Then the disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord. Jesus said to them again, “Peace to you. In the way that the Father has sent me, I am sending you.” Having said this, he breathed on them and told them, “Receive the Holy Spirit.” Whose sins you forgive, they stand forgiven; whose sins you retain, they stand retained. But Thomas, one of the Twelve, also called Didymus (which means Twin), was not with them when Jesus came. So the other disciples kept telling him, “We have seen the Lord!” But he told them, “I will never believe it unless I see the marks the nails made in his hands, and put my finger into those marks, and put my hand into his side.”

Jesus and Thomas

A week later his disciples were indoors again, and Thomas was with them. Though the doors were locked, Jesus came and stood among them and said, “Peace to you.” Then he said to Thomas, “Put your finger here; see my hands. Bring your hand and put it into my side. Do not be unbelieving any longer, but believing.” Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!” Jesus said to him, “Have you believed because you have seen me? Blessed are those who have believed without having seen.”

Why this book was written

Jesus did many other signs as well while the disciples looked on, signs that are not written down in this book. These, though, are written down so that you may believe Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and by believing have life in his name.

fields.title: John 21
fields.body_html:
Jesus appears by the sea

After this Jesus revealed himself to the disciples once more, by the Sea of Tiberias. It happened in this way. Simon Peter was there with Thomas (called Didymus, which means Twin), Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, Zebedee’s sons, and two more of his disciples. Simon Peter said to them, “I am going out fishing.” They answered, “We will come with you.” They went out and got into the boat, but all that night they caught nothing.

Just as day was breaking, Jesus stood on the shore, though the disciples did not realize that it was Jesus. So Jesus called out to them, “Friends, you have no fish to eat, have you?” They answered him, “No.” He said to them, “Throw the net out on the boat’s right side, and you will find fish.” So they threw it out, and now they could not haul it in because there were so many fish. Then that disciple whom Jesus loved told Peter, “It is the Lord!” Hearing that it was the Lord, Simon Peter tied his outer garment around himself, since he had stripped for work, and threw himself into the sea. The other disciples came in the boat, towing the net full of fish. They were not far out, only about 100 yards from land.

When they came ashore, they saw a charcoal fire already there, with fish laid on it, and bread. Jesus said to them, “Bring some of the fish that you have just caught.” So Simon Peter went aboard and hauled the net ashore, full of large fish, 153 of them. Even with so many, the net did not tear. Jesus said to them, “Come, eat your breakfast.” Not one of the disciples dared ask him, “Who are you?” They knew it was the Lord. Jesus came, took the bread and gave it to them, and the fish in the same way. This was now the third time that Jesus was revealed to the disciples after he had been raised from the dead.

Jesus and Peter

After they had eaten breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of John, do you love me more than these?” Peter said to him, “Yes, Lord, you know that I love you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my lambs.” A second time he asked him, “Simon, son of John, do you love me?” Peter said to him, “Yes, Lord, you know that I love you.” Jesus said to him, “Shepherd my sheep.” A third time he asked him, “Simon, son of John, do you love me?” Peter was hurt because Jesus asked him a third time, “Do you love me?” Peter replied, “Lord, you know everything; you know that I love you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep. Truly, truly, I tell you, when you were younger you fastened your own belt and went wherever you wished. But when you have grown old, you will stretch out your hands, and then someone else will fasten a belt on you and take you where you do not wish to go.” He said this to show by what kind of death Peter would glorify God. After saying this, he told him, “Follow me.”

The disciple whom Jesus loved

Peter turned around and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following them, the same disciple who at the supper had leaned back against Jesus’s chest and said, “Lord, who is it that is going to betray you?” When Peter saw him, he said to Jesus, “Lord, and what about him?” Jesus said to him, “If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you? As for you, follow me!” So the saying spread among the brothers and sisters that this disciple would not die. But Jesus had not told Peter that the disciple would not die; he had said, “If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you?” This is the disciple who is testifying about these things and who has written them, and we know his testimony is true. Jesus did many other things as well. If each one were written down, I suppose that even the world itself could not hold all the books that would be written.

fields.title: Conclusion
fields.body_html:
Jesus did many other things as well. If each one were written down, I suppose that even the world itself could not hold all the books that would be written.

— John 21:25

John ends by admitting that he has left almost everything out. It is a disarming last sentence for a book so carefully made, and an honest one. He has not tried to tell us everything Jesus did. He has chosen, from a life too large for all the books in the world, the handful of days and words that would let a reader see who Jesus is, and believe, and live.

The question the book leaves with you

Look back over the Gospel and it is full of people deciding what to do about Jesus. Andrew goes to fetch his brother. Nathanael, who doubted anything good could come from a place like Nazareth, ends the first chapter calling Jesus the Son of God. The Samaritan woman leaves her water jar at the well. A crowd that wanted bread walks away when Jesus offers himself instead, and he turns to the Twelve to ask whether they will go too. Peter answers for them all:

Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, to whom would we go? You have words that bring eternal life. We have believed, and we know, that you are the Holy One of God.”

— John 6:68–69

Others decide the opposite way. Some who see Lazarus walk out of his tomb go straight to the Pharisees, and from that day the council plots to kill the man who called him out. Pilate, who asks “What is truth?”, has the Truth standing in front of him and hands him over to be crucified. John does not soften this. Light has come into the world, and people respond to it.

The last person in the Gospel to come to faith is Thomas, who had said he would not believe unless he could touch the wounds. When Jesus offers them to him, he does not need to. He says the greatest words of faith in the book, “My Lord and my God!”, and Jesus answers with a blessing that reaches beyond the room and down the centuries to every reader of the Gospel: “Blessed are those who have believed without having seen.” That blessing is the book’s hope for you.

Life, not only information

John’s stated purpose has two halves: that you may believe, and that by believing you may have life. He means a life that begins now. In John, eternal life is not only life that lasts forever; it is the life of God himself, given to people while they are still on this earth. “Eternal life is this,” Jesus prays on his last night: “that they know you, the only true God, and the one you sent, Jesus Christ.”

That is why the farewell chapters (13 to 17) are so full of the word remain. Having shown us who Jesus is, John shows us what it is to live with him: to remain in him as a branch remains in the vine, to keep his word, to love one another as he has loved us, to receive the Spirit he promised, the Advocate who would be with his people when he had gone. The Gospel ends on a beach with a meal and a commission, not with a farewell. The risen Jesus says to Peter what he says to every disciple: “Follow me.”

Where to go from here

Readers have been preaching, praying and writing about John for nineteen centuries, and many of the best of them are in this library. A few places to begin:

  • On abiding in Christ (John 15). Andrew Murray’s The True Vine is a month of short readings on the vine and the branches; his Abide in Christ takes the single word “remain” and spends a whole book on it.
  • On being born again (John 3). J. C. Ryle’s sermon Are You Born Again? and D. L. Moody’s The New Birth both take up Jesus’s words to Nicodemus; Charles Finney’s God’s Love for a Sinning World preaches on John 3:16.
  • On the cross. John Newton’s Behold the Lamb of God (John 1:29), and two sermons on Jesus’s promise to draw all people to himself when he is lifted up (John 12:32): Spurgeon’s Christ Lifted Up and R. A. Torrey’s The Great Attraction.
  • On living water (John 4 and 7). Hudson Taylor’s Unfailing Springs and William J. Seymour’s River of Living Water.
  • On the promise of the Spirit (John 14). Martin Luther’s The Office of the Holy Spirit and A. W. Tozer’s How to Cultivate the Holy Spirit’s Companionship.
  • On faith and following. Alexander Maclaren’s Grace and Truth (John 1:17), Tozer’s He Must Increase (John 3:30), Ryle’s To Whom? (John 6:68), Horatius Bonar’s Faith in an Unseen Christ (John 20:29), and Spurgeon’s Lovest Thou Me? on the conversation by the lake (John 21:15–17).

You can also go the other way, from the text to the classics. Every reference to John in this library can be tapped to read the verse, and the Scripture pages gather, chapter by chapter, what the great writers of the church have said about each passage of this Gospel.

But the best next step may simply be to read John again. It is a book that rewards a second reading more than almost any other, because on the second time through you know, from the very first verse, what the people in the story are still finding out. And you may find that the question Jesus asked at the beginning has been waiting for you all along:

“What are you looking for?”

— John 1:38
